meta.title: PHP dangerous PATTERNS (non-function vulnerability classes)
meta.purpose: Language-level, input-shape, and semantic vulnerabilities that are NOT a single dangerous function call — the half a sink catalog misses. Each pattern says HOW to detect it (ast=node pattern, regex, query=XERJ, manual=reasoning) so the audit can claim coverage of patterns too.

patterns.title: Loose == / != comparison
patterns.attack: '0e123'==<'0e456' (magic hash), '0'==false, null==0, '1abc'==1, 'abc'==0 (pre-PHP8). Auth bypass when comparing secrets/hashes/tokens with == instead of ===.
patterns.detect: ast: binary_expression operator in {==,!=,<>}. Flag when either side is a hash()/md5()/sha1() call, a token/password/hmac variable, or a request value.
patterns.safe: === / !== ; hash_equals() for secrets; password_verify() for passwords.

patterns.title: switch() uses loose comparison
patterns.attack: switch($_GET['role']){case 0: admin...} — '0abc' or true loosely matches case 0.
patterns.detect: ast: switch_statement whose condition is a request value or unhashed string.
patterns.safe: match(true){...} (strict) or cast+validate the switch value first.

patterns.title: Magic-hash comparison (0e...)
patterns.attack: md5('240610708')=='0e462097431906509019562988736854'; two 0e-prefixed hashes are equal under ==. Password/token bypass.
patterns.detect: ast+manual: == between two hash outputs, or hash compared to a user value with ==.
patterns.safe: hash_equals(); never == on hashes.

patterns.title: strcmp/strcasecmp/strncmp with array arg returns NULL
patterns.attack: ?pw[]=x makes $_GET['pw'] an array; strcmp(array,$secret) returns NULL (+warning); if(strcmp(...)==0) => NULL==0 => TRUE => bypass.
patterns.detect: ast+query: strcmp-family call where an argument traces to a request value with no is_string()/is_scalar() guard.
patterns.safe: validate is_string() first; use hash_equals; check ===0 not ==0.

patterns.title: in_array/array_search without strict=true
patterns.attack: in_array('1abc',[1,2,3]) is TRUE loosely; in_array(0,['a','b']) TRUE pre-PHP8. Allow-list bypass.
patterns.detect: ast: in_array/array_search call with <3 args (strict omitted) or 3rd arg falsey.
patterns.safe: in_array($x,$arr,true).

patterns.title: Array injection via param[]=
patterns.attack: ?login[]=a or login[]=a in POST makes $_POST['login'] an ARRAY. Breaks string-typed sinks: preg_match(returns false), strcmp/hash(NULL), sql (Array->'Array'), and bypasses is_string()-less checks. Also DoS/logic.
patterns.detect: query+manual: request params used by string functions/SQL/regex without a preceding is_string()/is_scalar()/(string) cast or (array) normalisation.
patterns.safe: cast/validate every request param to the expected type; reject arrays where scalars expected.

patterns.title: SQL column truncation (silent, non-STRICT mode)
patterns.attack: Register user 'admin<55 spaces>x'; MySQL (non-strict) truncates to column length -> stored as 'admin' -> duplicate/overwrite admin account.
patterns.detect: manual+schema: INSERT/UPDATE of a user-controlled string into a VARCHAR(N) unique column without an explicit length check; requires column lengths.
patterns.safe: validate max length before insert; STRICT_ALL_TABLES; unique+trim checks.

patterns.title: Multibyte charset SQLi (addslashes/GBK bypass)
patterns.attack: In GBK/Big5, 0xbf27 + addslashes -> 0xbf5c27 which is a valid multibyte char + a free quote -> breaks out. Defeats addslashes/manual escaping.
patterns.detect: manual: manual escaping (addslashes/mysql_real_escape_string) with a connection charset set to a multibyte set instead of set_charset('utf8mb4').
patterns.safe: parameterized queries; mysqli::set_charset('utf8mb4').

patterns.title: ORDER BY / LIMIT / identifier injection
patterns.attack: ORDER BY $_GET['sort'] — identifiers can't be bound with placeholders; direct concat = injection.
patterns.detect: regex+query: ORDER BY/GROUP BY/LIMIT/table/column built from a request value (prepare can't bind these).
patterns.safe: allow-list of column names; map input->fixed identifier.

patterns.title: Second-order injection (stored then used raw)
patterns.attack: Value stored safely, later read from DB and concatenated into SQL/HTML/cmd without re-escaping. Taint 'launders' through storage.
patterns.detect: manual: a value read from DB/option/meta reaching a sink; the taint graph must treat storage reads as tainted for stored-then-used flows.
patterns.safe: escape at every sink, not just at input; treat DB reads as untrusted.

patterns.title: Mass assignment / register_globals emulation
patterns.attack: extract($_REQUEST) or foreach($_POST as $k=>$v){$$k=$v;} or $obj->fill($_POST) overwrites vars/columns (e.g. is_admin).
patterns.detect: ast: extract() / parse_str(1-arg) / variable_variable assignment ($$k) fed by a request array; object hydration from a raw request array.
patterns.safe: explicit allow-list of fields; never bulk-assign request data.

patterns.title: Variable variables $$x
patterns.attack: $$key where key is request-controlled -> arbitrary variable overwrite / info leak.
patterns.detect: ast: variable_name whose name is itself a variable (dynamic_variable_name) fed by request.
patterns.safe: array lookups with an allow-list, not $$.

patterns.title: Null-byte / poison-byte truncation
patterns.attack: ?file=secret.php%00.jpg truncates at NUL in include/file ops (pre-5.3.4); also %00 in strings splitting validators.
patterns.detect: manual+regex: file/path/validator using a request value without an explicit NUL/`\0` rejection; older PHP targets.
patterns.safe: reject \0; PHP>=5.3.4; realpath+allow-list.

patterns.title: Path traversal encodings
patterns.attack: ../, ..%2f, %2e%2e%2f, ....//, absolute-path override, unicode dot. Escapes an intended base dir.
patterns.detect: query+manual: file op / include with a request-derived path lacking realpath()-under-base or basename()+allow-list.
patterns.safe: realpath() then verify str_starts_with(base); basename+allow-list.

patterns.title: phar:// deserialization
patterns.attack: phar://attacker.jpg triggers unserialize of the Phar metadata via ANY file op (file_exists/getimagesize/fopen) on an attacker-controlled path -> POP chain.
patterns.detect: query+manual: any file op whose path can start with a user-controlled wrapper/scheme; combined with a gadget class present.
patterns.safe: validate/deny wrappers; Phar::interceptFileFuncs; check scheme.

patterns.title: TOCTOU file race (check-then-use)
patterns.attack: is_writable($f)/file_exists($f) then fopen/unlink($f) — attacker swaps the path (symlink) between check and use.
patterns.detect: ast+manual: a file predicate on a path followed by an operation on the same path in a privileged context.
patterns.safe: operate on fds (O_NOFOLLOW), atomic ops, avoid predictable temp paths.

patterns.title: Non-constant-time secret comparison
patterns.attack: if($mac == $expected) leaks byte-by-byte timing -> MAC/token forgery; also juggling.
patterns.detect: ast: == / != / strcmp on a variable named mac/sig/hmac/token/hash/nonce.
patterns.safe: hash_equals($known,$user).

patterns.title: is_numeric / intval / filter_var bypass
patterns.attack: is_numeric('0x1A'|'1e3'|' 12'|'+9') can be TRUE; (int)'123abc'=123; filter_var URL/EMAIL accepts javascript:, unusual hosts; is_numeric hex opens ID confusion.
patterns.detect: ast+manual: is_numeric/ctype_digit/intval/(int)/filter_var used as the ONLY validation on a security-relevant value.
patterns.safe: ctype_digit for digit-strings; FILTER + explicit flags; compare after cast+re-render.

patterns.title: empty()/isset() logic pitfalls
patterns.attack: empty('0') and empty(0) are TRUE -> a legit '0' input treated as missing; isset() true for null-coalesced; == in guards.
patterns.detect: manual: empty()/! on a value where '0'/0/'' are valid, in an auth/authorization/branch decision.
patterns.safe: === '' / array_key_exists / isset with explicit checks.

patterns.title: Regex anchor / multiline / dot bypass
patterns.attack: preg_match('/^allowed$/',$x) — $ matches before a trailing \n; with /m, ^/$ per line; . doesn't match \n so payload on a second line bypasses. Also \A\z vs ^$.
patterns.detect: regex+manual: a validation preg_match using ^...$ (not \A...\z) on a request value; check for /m and missing /s or /D.
patterns.safe: \A...\z anchors; /D; reject newlines.

patterns.title: PCRE returns false on backtrack-limit (not 0)
patterns.attack: On catastrophic backtracking preg_match returns FALSE, not 0; if(preg_match($bad,$x)) treats false as no-match, but code checking ==1 or !==false differs -> validator bypass + ReDoS.
patterns.detect: ast+manual: preg_match result used in a boolean/auth branch without ===1 / preg_last_error() check; user-influenced pattern or subject length.
patterns.safe: check ===1; bound input length; pcre.backtrack_limit.

patterns.title: Session fixation (no regenerate on auth)
patterns.attack: Attacker sets victim's session id pre-login; app doesn't session_regenerate_id(true) after auth -> session hijack.
patterns.detect: query+manual: a login/privilege-elevation path with no session_regenerate_id(true) after establishing identity.
patterns.safe: session_regenerate_id(true) on every privilege change.

patterns.title: Missing cookie security flags
patterns.attack: setcookie without HttpOnly/Secure/SameSite -> XSS theft / CSRF / MITM.
patterns.detect: ast: setcookie/setrawcookie/session_set_cookie_params with options lacking httponly|secure|samesite.
patterns.safe: set HttpOnly+Secure+SameSite=Lax/Strict.

patterns.title: State change without CSRF/nonce
patterns.attack: A state-changing handler reachable without a verified nonce/token -> CSRF.
patterns.detect: query: entry point performing a state change with NO nonce/token verification on the path (absence property — see the authz graph).
patterns.safe: verify a per-user, per-action nonce/CSRF token on every state change.

patterns.title: Wrong-context / incomplete output escaping
patterns.attack: htmlspecialchars without ENT_QUOTES inside an attribute; esc_html on a value placed in JS/URL/CSS context; double-encoding; json in <script> without JSON_HEX_TAG.
patterns.detect: manual: an escaper whose context (HTML text/attr/JS/URL/CSS) does not match the output position.
patterns.safe: context-correct escaper (attr vs html vs js vs url); ENT_QUOTES; JSON_HEX_* in <script>.

patterns.title: Open redirect
patterns.attack: header('Location: '.$_GET['next']) or redirect($url) to //evil.com, \evil, javascript:.
patterns.detect: ast+query: header('Location'..)/redirect with a request-derived target lacking an allow-list/same-host check.
patterns.safe: allow-list hosts; wp_safe_redirect; strip scheme/host.

patterns.title: Host / X-Forwarded trust
patterns.attack: Using $_SERVER['HTTP_HOST'] / X-Forwarded-For / X-Forwarded-Host for links, password-reset URLs, or IP allow-lists -> poisoning/spoof.
patterns.detect: regex: $_SERVER['HTTP_HOST'|'HTTP_X_FORWARDED_*'] used in a URL, email, or access decision.
patterns.safe: fixed site URL config; trust only vetted proxies.

patterns.title: @ error suppression hiding failures
patterns.attack: @unserialize / @file_get_contents / @$_GET hides errors that mask a security-relevant failure or type issue.
patterns.detect: ast: error_suppression_expression (@) on a security-relevant call.
patterns.safe: handle errors explicitly.

patterns.title: Unrestricted file upload -> exec
patterns.attack: Attacker uploads shell.php / .phtml / double-ext shell.php.jpg / MIME-spoofed / .htaccess; served from an executable dir.
patterns.detect: manual+query: move_uploaded_file/write into a web-served dir with extension/MIME derived from the upload and no allow-list / non-exec storage.
patterns.safe: random name; extension+content allow-list; store outside web root / non-exec.

patterns.title: User enumeration (distinct response/timing)
patterns.attack: Login/reset returns different message or timing for valid vs invalid users -> account enumeration.
patterns.detect: manual: auth/reset flows with user-existence-dependent branches in message or timing.
patterns.safe: uniform responses and timing.

patterns.title: escapeshellarg does NOT stop argument/option injection
patterns.attack: escapeshellarg only quotes a value so it can't start a NEW command — it does NOT stop the value being read as an OPTION. e.g. exec('tar '.escapeshellarg($f)) with $f='--checkpoint=1 --checkpoint-action=exec=sh evil' => tar runs a command. Same: rsync -e, mysql --, curl -o/-K, ffmpeg -f, git --upload-pack, find -exec, zip -T -TT, wget -O.
patterns.detect: ast+manual: an exec-family call whose arg is escapeshellarg($x) BUT $x is placed where the program accepts options (no `--` separator before it, or the value can begin with `-`) and $x is request-derived.
patterns.safe: place a literal `--` before user args; validate the value doesn't start with `-`; use array-form proc_open/exec with explicit argv; allow-list.

patterns.title: escapeshellcmd is weaker than escapeshellarg
patterns.attack: escapeshellcmd escapes shell metacharacters of a whole COMMAND but leaves spaces/quotes so arguments still split; it also lets option injection and unbalanced-quote tricks. Often misused as if it quoted an argument.
patterns.detect: ast: escapeshellcmd wrapping a value that is then used as an argument (not the whole command).
patterns.safe: escapeshellarg per-argument; argv-form; never escapeshellcmd for an argument.

patterns.title: Archive extraction path traversal (Zip Slip)
patterns.attack: ZipArchive::extractTo($dir) / PharData / tar writes each entry using the entry's own path; an entry named ../../wp-config.php or /etc/... escapes $dir -> arbitrary write/overwrite (RCE if a .php lands in webroot). Symlink entries read/write outside too.
patterns.detect: query+manual: extractTo / archive extraction of an attacker-supplied archive without validating each entry path stays under the target (realpath prefix check).
patterns.safe: iterate entries, reject absolute/`..`/symlink names, realpath-under-base each before write.

patterns.title: phar:// via a file op on a user path (already-catalogued file ops)
patterns.attack: Any file op (file_exists/getimagesize/fopen/is_file/md5_file) on phar://uploaded.jpg triggers unserialize of Phar metadata -> POP chain. The 'safe-looking' file op is the trigger.
patterns.detect: query: file-read/exists ops whose path can carry a user-controlled stream wrapper (no scheme allow-list).
patterns.safe: validate scheme; Phar::interceptFileFuncs(); deny phar://.
